$note: How a daemon release is decided (plan §9; E4.S2): release-please reads the conventional commits under src_daemon/
since the last daemon-v* tag and opens a pull request that bumps src_daemon/version.txt (the `simple` strategy's
version file — src_daemon/Directory.Build.props stamps every assembly from it) and writes src_daemon/CHANGELOG.md.
MERGING that pull request decides the release; the next run of release-please.yml cuts the tag daemon-v<version>
and a DRAFT release, and the tag starts release.yml.

$bootstrap: THE FIRST RELEASE IS 0.1.0 EXACTLY, from two settings that only work together. Read in release-please's own code as
bundled by release-please-action v5.0.0 (dist/index.js at 45996ed1), not recalled:
1. The manifest says `"src_daemon": "0.0.0"`, the same as version.txt. Manifest.buildPullRequests backfills a
'previous release' from the manifest only when the version there is NOT 0.0.0 (`toString() !== '0.0.0'`, with
the log line 'No latest release found ... but a previous version (X) was specified in the manifest'). A manifest
saying 0.1.0 would therefore be taken as ALREADY RELEASED and the first release would be 0.1.1 or 0.2.0 —
0.1.0 would never exist. 0.0.0 is release-please's own spelling of 'never released', and it keeps the manifest
and version.txt equal at every moment (ReleaseWorkflowTests holds them equal).
2. `initial-version` is 0.1.0. With no previous release BaseStrategy.buildNewVersion returns
initialReleaseVersion(), which is `initial-version` when set and otherwise 1.0.0; the `simple` strategy does not
override it. A `Release-As:` footer would still win over both — none may be used for the first release.
After daemon-v0.1.0 the release pull request has written 0.1.0 into both files and `initial-version` is never read
again. Every daemon commit in history is in range for the first changelog (no bootstrap-sha), which is the point.

$scope: WHAT IS A DAEMON RELEASE IS DECIDED BY THE PACKAGE PATH. release-please hands the package `src_daemon` only the commits
that touch a file under `src_daemon/` (its CommitSplit), so a commit touching only `.github/` or root build files
(global.json, Directory.*.props) is never a daemon release — ship such a change with the next daemon change. There is
deliberately NO `exclude-paths`: an exclude path outside every package path can never remove a commit the split already
kept out, so the key would be inert while reading as a guarantee (E4 review, 2026-10-03; ReleaseConfigTests holds
the package-path rule and the absence of the key).
$versioning: BEFORE 1.0.0: `bump-minor-pre-major` makes a breaking change (`feat!:`, a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer) bump the MINOR,
not jump to 1.0.0 — release-please's default; `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major` stays false, so a `feat:` is a minor
too (every epic ends in a minor release, plan §16) and a `fix:` a patch.
